dial.summary: 4/8 indicators remain supportive on November 18 — Global M2 at $104.3T (Sep record, Oct data pending), ISM Manufacturing at 55.5 (10th consecutive expansion month), Fed Balance Sheet flat at $6.77T, and BTC perp funding at 0.0043% (near-zero) signal a deleveraged market in classic accumulation conditions; DXY at 103.70 (19-month highs, above 100 threshold) is the primary headwind; real yields ticked to 2.91% but 4-week trend is flat, 2s10s stable at +29bps — macro fundamentals intact with FOMC minutes released today and Oct PCE due Nov 25.

indicators.name: Global Liquidity (Global M2)
indicators.note: MacroMicro G4 aggregate (US/Euro Zone/China/Japan) at ~$104.3T as of September 2026 (104,317.08B per MacroMicro series); October G4 data not yet published as of November 18, 2026 — typically updated mid-to-late November following the reference month; US M2 $23.41T in Sep 2026 (+5.7% YoY per FRED H.6, next release Nov 24); 4-week Aug→Sep G4 change: +$0.64T (+0.6%), above flat threshold — trend UP; status supportive (4-week G4 trend up, no YoY contraction); held unchanged pending October G4 publication.

indicators.name: ISM Manufacturing PMI
indicators.note: October 2026 ISM Manufacturing PMI at 55.5% (released November 2, 2026), beating consensus 54.7%, up 1.0pp from September's 54.5%; 10th consecutive expansion month; Production sub-index 59.0 (highest since Nov 2021), New Orders 55.5, Employment 52.4; Prices Paid 75.2 (down from Sep's 77.9, still elevated); 4-week trend UP (Sep 54.5 → Oct 55.5, +1.0pp); status supportive (above 50 and rising); next ISM Manufacturing release December 1, 2026; held unchanged — October 55.5 is the current monthly reading.

indicators.name: DXY (US Dollar Index)
indicators.note: ICE DXY spot ~103.70 as of November 18, 2026 (CNBC: 103.703 intraday Nov 18 at 52-week high of 103.78; Trading Economics: 103.636 as of Nov 17; prior close Nov 17: 103.485 per ChainCatcher); 4-week trend UP — from ~101.5–101.8 on October 14 to ~103.70 on November 18, net +~1.9–2.2%, well above the 0.5% flat threshold; hot October CPI (+0.4% MoM, Nov 10), hawkish Fed repricing, and strong October retail sales drove DXY to 19-month highs; status headwind (DXY above 100 — must fall below 97.5 for supportive); FRED DTWEXBGS network-restricted in this environment — ICE spot corroborated via CNBC, Trading Economics, and ChainCatcher.

indicators.name: Real Yields (US10Y - CPI)
indicators.note: 10-year TIPS real yield (DFII10) at 2.91% on November 13, 2026 (most recent FRED print available; prior readings: Nov 12 2.86%, Nov 10 2.78%, Nov 9 2.66%); FRED API network-restricted — values sourced from thetrading.tools and macrodial.org aggregators; 4-week trend FLAT — from approximately 2.85–2.90% on October 14 to 2.91% on November 13, net +1 to +6bps within flat threshold (<5bps relative is flat); status neutral (above 2% but flat — headwind requires BOTH rising trend AND above 2%; a 5bp move from the Oct 14 base does not meet the rising-trend criterion); 52-week range approximately 1.72%–2.95%.

indicators.name: 2s10s Yield Curve
indicators.note: 2s10s spread at approximately +27–29bps as of November 13–16, 2026 (CappNotes Nov 16: ~29bps as short-term yields fell faster; Treasury par curve Nov 13: 27bps; YieldCurve.pro Nov 10: 25bps); 4-week trend FLAT — from approximately +28–32bps on October 14 to +27–29bps on Nov 13–16, net change approximately -1 to -5bps, within flat threshold; status neutral (positive spread, curve not inverted — headwind requires < -50bps); FOMC minutes released November 18 at 2:00 PM ET may shift front-end yields and alter the spread by next session; 52-week range 20 to 74bps.

indicators.name: Fed Balance Sheet
indicators.note: WALCL approximately $6.77T for week ended November 11, 2026 (+$10B from prior week per American Action Forum tracker; prior weekly readings: Nov 4 $6.748T, Oct 28 $6.75T, Oct 14 $6.756T); FRED API network-restricted — figure sourced from AAF and thetrading.tools trackers; 4-week change Oct 14→Nov 11: +~$14B, essentially flat; YoY +$178B (+2.7%); status supportive (flat with slight YoY growth, QT ended, balance sheet drifting up with reserve demand); next H.4.1 release November 19, 2026 (covering week ended November 18).

indicators.name: BTC Funding Rates (perps avg)
indicators.note: CoinGlass BTC page shows OI-weighted funding rate at 0.0043% per 8h as of November 18, 2026 (labeled neutral by CoinGlass; ~4.7% annualized); prior OI-weighted reading Nov 17: -0.0004%; CoinPerps: +0.0029% per 8h; Binance briefly -0.0022% on Nov 16; 30-day trend FLAT — mid-October rates near zero, brief negative dip Nov 16, back near zero Nov 18, no sustained directional move; status supportive (0.0043% well below the 0.04% headwind threshold; near-zero funding in a compressed total market reflects deleveraging and cleared speculation, a classic accumulation signal).

indicators.name: Stablecoin Dominance
indicators.note: Stablecoin market cap $284.159B as of November 18, 2026 (DefiLlama; USDT $175.344B, 61.66% dominance within stables); total crypto market cap ~$2.31–2.34T (Au79 Macro Nov 16; BTC dominance 58.2–59.1%); implied stablecoin dominance ~12.3% ($284.159B / $2.31T); 30-day trend UP — October 14 dominance ~10.5–10.8%, November 18 ~12.3%, net +~1.5–1.8pp; status neutral — headwind requires rising dominance AND rising TOTAL simultaneously; TOTAL has contracted from ~$2.6T (Oct 14) to ~$2.31T so headwind condition not met; rising stablecoin share reflects risk-off repositioning and sidelined capital during BTC pullback, not broad fundamental deterioration.

upcoming.title: Initial Jobless Claims (week ended November 15, 2026)
upcoming.note: DOL releases weekly initial jobless claims at 8:30 AM ET; key weekly labor read ahead of the Thanksgiving-week data lull and the ~November 29 FOMC blackout period; a sustained trend above 220K would add dovish counter-pressure to the December 9 hike case; next NFP release December 4 (November data), arriving just 5 days before the December 9 FOMC decision.

upcoming.title: Philadelphia Fed Manufacturing Index (November 2026)
upcoming.note: Federal Reserve Bank of Philadelphia releases November 2026 Manufacturing Business Outlook Survey at 8:30 AM ET; first-look at November manufacturing activity ahead of the December 1 ISM Manufacturing PMI; a positive print above 0 would reinforce the October ISM signal at 55.5; released on the third Thursday of the month, same day as jobless claims.

upcoming.title: S&P Global Flash PMIs (November 2026)
upcoming.note: S&P Global releases flash estimates for US Manufacturing and Services PMIs for November 2026 at 9:45 AM ET; first real-time read on November business activity ahead of the December 1 ISM Manufacturing PMI; a Services print above 55 would reinforce the sticky-inflation narrative heading into the December 9 FOMC decision; ISM Manufacturing was 55.5 for October (10th straight expansion); Euro area flash PMIs also released same morning.

upcoming.title: Conference Board Consumer Confidence (November 2026)
upcoming.note: Conference Board releases November 2026 Consumer Confidence Index at 10:00 AM ET; released last Tuesday of each month; tracks consumer sentiment on current conditions and 6-month expectations; a deterioration from October's level would signal cracks in the consumer spending backdrop ahead of the November 25 PCE release; expectations sub-index is a leading indicator for future consumption and GDP.

upcoming.title: GDP Q3 2026 — Second Estimate
upcoming.note: BEA releases Q3 2026 GDP second estimate at 8:30 AM ET (Thanksgiving-week compressed schedule, Wednesday before Thursday Nov 26 Thanksgiving); revises the advance estimate from late October; watch consumer spending and PCE deflator revisions for any upside that would further seal the December 9 hike case; released same day as October PCE — double inflation-and-growth print on thin pre-holiday liquidity.

upcoming.title: PCE Inflation / Personal Income (October 2026)
upcoming.note: BEA releases October 2026 Personal Income and Outlays (including PCE Price Index) at 8:30 AM ET; PCE is the Fed's preferred inflation gauge — a hot reading above +0.3% MoM core PCE would seal the December 9 FOMC hike after October CPI surprised at +0.4% MoM; this is the last major inflation print before the ~November 29 FOMC blackout and the December 9 decision; Thanksgiving-week release means thin liquidity; released same day as Q3 GDP second estimate.
